articles.title: Watchdogs flag ballot violations, vote-buying as BARMM polls near end
articles.summary: Namfrel and LENTE raise alarm over reports of pre-shaded ballots, vote-buying, voter coercion, and armed people at voting centers as the first BARMM parliamentary election progresses

blocks.text: PRE-SHADED BALLOT. The Commission on Elections reports ballots in several voting precincts in Maluso, Basilan, have been pre-shaded ahead of the Bangsamoro parliamentary elections on September 14, 2026.
Commission on Elections
Namfrel and LENTE raise alarm over reports of pre-shaded ballots, vote-buying, voter coercion, and armed people at voting centers as the first BARMM parliamentary election progresses

items: Election watchdogs reported significant irregularities during the first parliamentary elections in the Bangsamoro region, including pre-shaded ballots, vote-buying, and armed individuals in voting centers.

Concerns were raised about the integrity of the voting process, with many voters reportedly not able to cast their ballots freely and in secrecy due to unauthorized assistance and violations of ballot handling procedures.
Despite these issues, many polling places opened on time and the elections proceeded, with voting scheduled to end at 7 pm, followed by counting and canvassing.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

CAGAYAN DE ORO, Philippines – By early afternoon, the first parliamentary election in the Bangsamoro region was still hours from closing, but election watchdogs were already compiling a troubling picture.

Reports of alleged pre-shaded ballots, voters being told how to vote, money changing hands, and armed people inside voting centers raised questions about whether some voters in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM) were able to cast their ballots freely and in secrecy.

The National Citizens’ Movement for Free Elections (Namfrel) and Legal Network for Truthful Elections (LENTE) both reported irregularities as voting progressed, although they said polling was orderly in many places.
Namfrel, in an early afternoon bulletin, cited allegations of pre-shaded ballots, unauthorized handling of ballots, attempts to bypass voting procedures, and the blocking of accredited observers.

The election monitor said it was “deeply concerned by reports of violence, ballot fraud, and obstruction of accredited observers in several localities” even as it called on candidates, security forces, and elections officials to “help ensure that the remainder of the electoral exercise is peaceful and calls on voters and volunteers alike to remain vigilant.”
LENTE, in a 2 pm bulletin, reported vote-buying, ballot secrecy violations, unauthorized assistance and firearms inside voting centers as voting progressed in the first BARMM parliamentary elections.

The allegations could not be immediately independently verified. The Commission on Elections (Comelec), however, earlier ordered the replacement of ballots in Maluso, Basilan, and placed the town under its control after pre-shaded ballots were discovered.

Assisted voting was among the most widespread concerns. LENTE said 187 of 501 reports involving voter assistance, or about 37%, concerned assisted voting. It warned excessive or unauthorized assistance could compromise ballot secrecy and allow those helping voters to substitute their own choices.

“A major issue to emerge from the BARMM elections thus far is the vulnerability of voters’ ability to freely choose their own representatives, with the sanctity of the ballot repeatedly violated and the assisted voting process abused across several areas LENTE monitored,” the group said.
LENTE added, “In its worst form, an assistor is no longer assisting the voter at all but substituting their own choice for the true will of the electorate.”

In 137 of 492 reports, or 28%, voters did not personally feed their ballots into automated counting machines. Electoral board members were reported to have done so in 119 cases, contrary to election rules.

In Maguindanao del Norte, some voters reportedly left polling places before their ballots were fed into machines, allowing watchers to complete the process. In 41 reports, people assisting voters had helped more than the legal limit of three voters, LENTE said.
The watchdog also recorded 19 reports of vote-buying and 27 cases of partisan political activity by electoral board members.
Security concerns included seven reports of people carrying firearms inside voting centers, including three incidents each in Talitay, Maguindanao del Norte, and Marawi City, Lanao del Sur.
Namfrel separately reported an intimidation and shooting incident at Pilot Central School in Cotabato City, where a volunteer also witnessed pre-shaded ballots.

In Sultan Kudarat, Maguindanao del Norte, a Namfrel volunteer reported seeing an electoral board member shade multiple official ballots and feed most of them into a vote-counting machine without voters present. Another volunteer reported receiving a pre-shaded ballot in Datu Abdullah Sangki, Maguindanao del Sur.

Namfrel also reported delays in election materials in Al-Barka, Basilan, because of security concerns involving armed people along transport routes. Some electoral boards were still being deployed as late as 10:20 am.
Despite the reports, Namfrel said most polling places it observed opened on time, with electoral boards, voting machines and election materials in place.
Voting is scheduled to end at 7 pm, followed by counting and canvassing. The elections are the first parliamentary polls in BARMM since the autonomous region was created in 2019. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Who owns ‘Elbows Up’? Canadian companies trying to cash in on patriotic slogan
articles.summary: From the hockey rink to the political arena, the phrase “Elbows Up” has become part of the Canadian lexicon — and now a number of businesses are trying to cash in on it.

image.caption: A hardware store in Hammonds Plains, N.S., displays 'Elbows Up' T-shirts. (Aly Thomson/CBC)

blocks.text: Nova Scotia·New
From the hockey rink to the political arena, the phrase “Elbows Up” has become part of the Canadian lexicon — and now a number of businesses are trying to cash in on it.
A dozen companies have applied to trademark the phrase

There are roughly a dozen applications listed on the Canadian Intellectual Property Office’s trademarks database to have the exclusive right to “Elbows Up,” with companies seeking to emblazon the slogan on everything from clothing to beer cans, bumper stickers and dietary supplements.
But the bulk of the applications, many of which were submitted over a year ago, have been met with objections from the office due to the phrase being “nondistinctive.”
Trademark and copyright lawyer Reagan Seidler said the office appears to have taken an official position that "Elbows Up" cannot function as a brand because it has become a patriotic symbol.
“They are of the opinion that nobody in Canada should be able to own the phrase,” said Seidler, who works with Smart and Biggar in Toronto.

“The trademarks office is of the view that if you see Elbows Up on a T-shirt, you're not going to think Elbows Up is the company name or its slogan. Like 'Just Do It.' You're going to think that is just repeating the kind of messaging that's come from the Prime Minister's Office and elsewhere.”

“Elbows Up” has been around for decades, first used to describe the playing style of legendary Canadian NHLer Gordie Howe, who was known to raise his elbows to protect himself and fend off opponents on the ice.
But early last year, the meaning shifted.

As the trade war with the U.S. heated up, actor Mike Myers appeared on Saturday Night Live and as the cast was waving goodbye, he unzipped his vest to display a shirt declaring that “Canada is not for sale.” He then gestured to his elbows and mouthed “elbows up.”
Not long after, Prime Minister Mark Carney released a campaign video with Myers, standing on the edge of a hockey rink, and ending with the pair repeating the phrase.
Seidler said it’s not unusual for companies to jump to trademark a moment or catchy expression, pointing to “very demure, very mindful,” made famous by a woman on TikTok.
But he’s never seen companies try to capitalize on a political event.
“It is very rare for the trademarks office to say, in principle, a phrase should not be owned by any particular company,” said Seidler.

“And they reference in their objections general news coverage of how the phrase has been used as their basis to say that elbows up inherently will not function as a brand name in the minds of Canadians.”
Mark Howe, son of “Mr. Elbows,” as he was also known, said he’s not surprised that people are trying to trademark Elbows Up, noting it’s a “very marketable thing.”

The Howe family is no stranger to trademarks. The Howe Foundation owns the trademarks for Gordie Howe, Mr. Hockey and Mrs. Hockey, mostly as a way to raise funds for the charitable organization, he said.
In fact, Mark Howe said officials had to ask permission to use his father’s name on the Gordie Howe International Bridge, which opened earlier this year.
“It's business. And I would like to think somebody would try to trademark it.… I would be shocked actually if somebody didn’t try to go after it,” said Howe in an interview.
Mark Howe said despite his father’s reputation on the ice, he was a respectful family man who would be appreciative of the hoopla surrounding “Elbows Up” and a namesake bridge.

“He'd be grateful and he'd be humble. But as soon as everything just kind of drifted away, he would look forward to being with his family, his grandkids, being out fishing, golfing, doing something like that,” said Howe.
The Canadian Intellectual Property Office declined an interview request, saying in a statement that it cannot provide information about applications.
Seidler said it has been interesting watching the “Elbows Up” phenomenon play out.

“I do think it's amusing to watch every time a phrase hits the public domain, the swath of people that will move in to try to monopolize that phrase and capitalize on it. It's a natural instinct,” he said.

“The more interesting part of the story is that the trademark office has taken the principled position that Elbows Up is not capable of serving, in their view, as a trademark and in that sense, reserving the right of all Canadians to use that phrase as this trade war continues.”

articles.title: Malaysian boy acquitted for murder of schoolgirl on grounds of insanity
articles.summary: The killing of the 16-year-old nearly a year ago had shocked Malaysia and sparked debate about social media.

blocks.text: A Malaysian teenage boy charged with the high-profile murder of a female schoolmate has been acquitted, with the judge finding the boy was mentally unsound during the incident.
He had fatally stabbed Yap Shing Xuen in a toilet at their secondary school on the outskirts of the capital Kuala Lumpur.
The killing of the 16-year-old girl had shocked Malaysia and sparked debate about the effects of social media on children.

Police previously had said they suspected social media could have influenced the boy, who was 14 at the time. The case was seen to have spurred authorities to limit children's access to social media, which began earlier this year.
The boy - who cannot be named under Malaysian law as he is still a minor - had pleaded not guilty to the murder charge.
During the trial defence lawyers did not deny that the boy killed the girl, but argued that he had suffered from poor mental health for years and asked for his acquittal on the grounds of insanity.
An expert witness, a psychiatrist, testified that the boy had schizophrenia, and had suffered from mental illness and experienced delusions since he was nine years old.

The boy's condition was said to have worsened during the pandemic and when he eventually returned to school. Lawyers had said that the boy would need medication for the rest of his life to manage symptoms.
On Monday the judge ruled that the boy would be acquitted, but also ordered for him to be detained and to receive treatment at a psychiatric hospital.
He will stay at the hospital until he is deemed fit to be released back to society, and would likely be subject to yearly assessments.
A defence lawyer told reporters on Monday that upon hearing the verdict, the boy appeared "neutral in emotion, but he understands what is going on, [that] it's a very serious matter".
The trial and verdict hearings were held in a closed court, which meant that the public and media could not attend.
The case has profoundly shocked Malaysia and sparked a nationwide conversation about the negative effects of social media on children.
Much of this conversation was triggered by the contents of a note that police had found on the boy at the time of his arrest, which was leaked online and widely circulated.
Some people had compared the case to the Netflix series Adolescence, which featured a storyline about a young boy killing a female schoolmate and explored the theme of online radicalisation.
Last year, the country's Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim was asked about the case as well as other recent cases of violence in schools.
He was quoted by local media as saying that "almost all of these issues stem from the use of mobile phones and social media", and vowed to look into stricter measures.
Authorities have since put in place new rules which they say will protect children and reduce their exposure to harmful online content.
Since June, Malaysia has banned all children under the age of 16 from having accounts on major social media platforms.
Additional reporting by Diyana Nawwar

articles.title: Meet Joaquin Tovera, the La Salle rookie who looks like UAAP’s next big thing
articles.summary: Rookie guard Joaquin Tovera shines in his debut for defending champion La Salle, wasting no time making his mark with his scoring prowess

blocks.text: ROOKIE. Joaquin Tovera in action for the La Salle Green Archers in the UAAP Season 89 men's basketball tournament.
UAAP
Rookie guard Joaquin Tovera shines in his debut for defending champion La Salle, wasting no time making his mark with his scoring prowess

items: Joaquin Tovera made an impressive debut for La Salle in the UAAP, scoring 22 points and contributing significantly to the team's victory over NU Bulldogs.
Tovera, a product of Chino Hills High School, has a strong basketball background, including international experience with the Gilas Pilipinas Youth program, where he excelled as a scorer.

Despite initially committing to UP, Tovera transferred to La Salle, where he is expected to develop into a key player alongside the team's veteran core, with the coaching staff noting his coachability and adaptability.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.
MANILA, Philippines – Joaquin Tovera did not take long to make his presence felt in the UAAP.

In his first game for defending champion La Salle, the 18-year-old guard looked right at home, exploding for 22 points to go with 3 steals in just 14 minutes as the Green Archers escaped the NU Bulldogs, 89-87, in their UAAP Season 89 men’s basketball tournament opener on Sunday, September 13.
For much of the game, Tovera looked like the best player on the floor, repeatedly blowing past NU guards Reinhard Jumamoy and Tebol Garcia, both of whom tried to get under his skin.
“At first I was nervous, but when I stepped on the court, I just wanted to show what I got,” said Tovera.

blocks.caption: Meet Joaquin Tovera, the La Salle rookie who looks like UAAP’s next big thing

blocks.text: “I think he was a bit nervous, but he got his bearings. It’s his first time playing in front of a crowd like this,” La Salle head coach Topex Robinson said. “I guess he just soaked up the experience. It’s going to get a lot tougher from here on, but he knows that.”
Tovera’s debut was impressive on its own, but his resume suggests there is much more to come.
The Filipino-American guard attended Chino Hills High School in California, the same basketball program that produced NBA stars Lonzo and LaMelo Ball.
Tovera made a name for himself with his explosive scoring, including a 47-point outburst against Etiwanda High School in a Baseline League game.
He also played for Fil-Am Nation Select on the competitive youth and travel circuits alongside fellow Filipino-American players based in the United States.
Representing Fil-Am Nation in this year’s NBTC tournament, Tovera averaged 27.7 points, 6.3 rebounds, and 5.7 assists per game.
Tovera also represented the Philippines internationally, emerging as a major force in the Gilas Pilipinas Youth program.
He won tournament MVP honors in the FIBA U18 Asia Cup SEABA Qualifiers after averaging 16.4 points, 4.0 assists, and 3.0 steals per game.
According to Robinson, it is what Tovera is expected to do with La Salle in the UAAP.
The La Salle coach has been particularly impressed by how quick the teenager has embraced the challenge of learning the team’s championship-proven system.

“I guess what really kind of stood out is the way he’s really been coachable,” Robinson said. “He was asking questions, especially with the veterans and other coaches. I guess we could see that he’s really making his way to adapt to our system. We don’t have to force him to do that, but he was the one asking those questions. That’s really huge for us.”
Tovera’s ability to contribute, even as a rookie, has also given La Salle another dynamic piece alongside its veteran core.

“Him scoring that much and contributing a lot on both ends helped us a lot. Having a young guy [playing well] together with our veterans is really going to be a big help for us moving forward,” Robinson added.
Before enrolling at La Salle, Tovera initially committed to play for the UP Fighting Maroons.
He even saw action for UP in the FilOil EcoOil Preseason Cup in June, serving as a backup to Rey Remogat.

Tovera averaged 5.0 points, 1.7 rebounds, and 3.3 assists during his brief stint with the Fighting Maroons. On his 18th birthday, however, he de-committed from UP and made the surprising move to La Salle, which caught many in the league by surprise.

Tovera was once viewed as the heir apparent to Remogat, who will leave UP at the end of Season 89. Instead, he landed at La Salle, where he is now being groomed as a potential successor to Jacob Cortez and the future leader of a program that has won two of the last three UAAP championships.
Robinson knows Tovera is still developing, though, and the La Salle coach is giving the teenager room to learn, make mistakes, and understand the game at the collegiate level.

“He’s young. He’s only 18. He’s going to make those young mistakes,” Robinson said. “What we just try to remind him is that everybody is allowed to make a mistake. You’ll get the support that you need. Hopefully, it’s going to lighten the process and the load on his shoulders.” – Rappler.com

articles.title: Amazon suspends use of cargo carrier whose plane careened off Miami runway
articles.summary: The Boeing 767 came in fast on Sept. 6 and then barreled roughly 396 metres past the end of the runway and smashed into a van carrying workers at a plane cleaning company.

image.caption: Workers inspect an Amazon cargo plane two days after it overshot a runway at Miami International Airport, Tuesday, Sept. 8, 2026, in Miami. (Rebecca Blackwell/The Associated Press)

blocks.text: World·New
The Boeing 767 came in fast on Sept. 6 and then barreled roughly 396 metres past the end of the runway and smashed into a van carrying workers at a plane cleaning company.
North Carolina-based 21 had flown packages for Amazon since 2024
Amazon said Sunday that it has suspended its partnership with 21 Air after one of the cargo carrier's planes loaded with Amazon packages careened off a Miami runway last week and killed five people.

The Boeing 767 came in fast on Sept. 6 and then barreled roughly 396 metres past the end of the runway and smashed into a van carrying workers at a plane cleaning company. All five people who died were in the van. Five others were hurt.

items: Pilot of Amazon plane flagged excessive speed before deadly Miami crash, investigators say

blocks.text: "After the tragic incident last weekend, we've spent time supporting the investigation and reviewing some of the surrounding circumstances, and we've decided to pause our operations with 21 Air, the operator of Flight 7598," Amazon spokesperson Kelly Nantel said a statement. "We'll continue working to support the investigation and everyone affected."
North Carolina-based 21 had flown packages for Amazon since 2024. The company didn't immediately respond Sunday to a request for comment about Amazon's decision.
U.S. investigators provide update on deadly Amazon plane crash

The jet's ownership history, weather conditions at the airport, maintenance records and operations by 21 Air were expected to be reviewed by investigators with the National Transportation Safety Board.
Flight information released by the NTSB on Sept. 9 revealed one of the pilots warned his counterpart they were going too fast as they approached for landing and after touchdown.

The cockpit audio recordings also captured a series of automated warnings from the plane about the speed of descent and the approaching terrain. The full transcript of the cockpit conversation won't be released until later in the investigation.

The 32-year-old Boeing was originally built to carry passengers and flew for several airlines in foreign countries for more than two decades before being converted to a cargo plane in 2015, according to flight-tracking site Flightradar24.

articles.title: Russia hits passenger train on Ukraine's border with Poland, just misses 'diplomatic train'
articles.summary: The train, on a route frequently used by foreign delegations returning from Kyiv, was attacked just two kilometres from the Polish border, Ukraine's railway operator said.

image.caption: Firefighters extinguish a car of a passenger train hit by a Russian drone strike at a railway station, amid Russia's attack on Ukraine, in Lutsk, Ukraine September 12, 2026. (Reuters)

blocks.text: World·New
The train, on a route frequently used by foreign delegations returning from Kyiv, was attacked just two kilometres from the Polish border, Ukraine's railway operator said.
No casualties were reported

A Russian drone hit a passenger train on Ukraine's border with NATO member Poland on Sunday, ‌shortly after former British Prime Minister Boris Johnson and other European diplomats had used the same line.
No casualties were reported.

"This wasn’t our train, but ​the one just minutes after us by the border crossing. It was ​evacuated as the drone approached and no one was hurt," Carl Bildt, former Sweden's Prime Minister said on X.

items: Deadly Russian strikes hit Ukraine after Putin's warning to European leaders

blocks.text: He and other politicians were returning to Europe by train after attending a conference ​in Kyiv.

"It is entirely possible that the Russian drone's intended target was the diplomatic train, which ⁠departed the station earlier than scheduled ⁠after train timetables were adjusted in real time because of ‌the constant threat of Russian strikes," Ukraine's railway operator, Ukrzaliznytsia, said on Telegram.
Boris Johnson, who was also on the train that left the station shortly before the strike, condemned the attack as "random and senseless" in a post on Instagram.
With the front line largely static, both Moscow and Kyiv have intensified long-distance ⁠strikes in recent weeks to try to shift momentum in the war.
Polish foreign minister Radoslaw Sikorski described Russia's increasing attacks on NATO's doorstep as "an escalation."
Earlier on Sunday a truck less than a kilometre from Ukraine's border with Poland was also hit, prompting ‌the Dorohusk-Yahodyn crossing point to briefly halt operations, according to border guards.
Russia's Defence Ministry said it had targeted infrastructure facilitating military cargoes from Europe in Western Ukraine.

Russia has begun targeting Ukraine's border crossings with its Western allies in recent weeks, part of a growing campaign by both sides to erode the other's economic infrastructure more than ​four years into Russia's invasion.
Russia reports strike near Zaporizhzhia nuclear power plant
Overnight, hostilities showed no signs of letting up.

In the Russian-held part of Ukraine's southeastern Zaporizhzhia ⁠region, the head of Russia's state nuclear energy company Rosatom accused Ukraine of striking fuel trucks close to the Zaporizhzhia ⁠nuclear power station, Europe's largest.

The Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant has been controlled by Russia since March 2022, and remains close ⁠to ⁠the front line. A Ukrainian military spokesperson did ​not immediately respond to a request for comment.
Zelenskyy says war holds no 'win-win' scenario for Russia and Ukraine

In Russia itself, the mayor of the city of Nizhnekamsk, in the Volga River ​region of Tatarstan, said that "civilian and industrial" ⁠targets in the city had been struck by Ukrainian drones, causing at least two deaths and several more injuries.
Mayor Radmir Belyaev did not clarify which targets had been struck, but the city hosts a major oil refinery which has been attacked in the past.
Ukrainian authorities did not immediately comment on the strike on Nizhekamsk, but did say they had struck another refinery in the southern ⁠Krasnodar region.

articles.title: BIR removes VAT on system loss charges in power bills
articles.summary: No more VAT on allowable system loss charges.

blocks.text: September 14, 2026 | 4:49pm
The sunset from the eastern side of Metro Manila silhouettes Meralco power lines supplying electricity to the area as seen on May 15, 2026.
The STAR / Walter Bollozos

MANILA, Philippines — Electricity consumers will no longer pay the 12% value-added tax on allowable system loss charges, after the Bureau of Internal Revenue excluded the charge from the VAT base of power companies.

Under Revenue Memorandum Circular No. 97-2026 issued Monday, September 14, the BIR recognized allowable system loss as a government-mandated pass-through cost rather than part of the gross sales of generation companies, the National Grid Corp. of the Philippines and distribution utilities.
This means the allowable system loss charge, within the cap set by the ERC, will no longer be subject to the 12% VAT.

"Every peso saved by consumers counts. This may be one part of a broader effort to bring down electricity costs, but it is a relief that can be implemented under existing law," BIR Commissioner Charlito Martin Mendoza said.

The circular confirms an ERC resolution approved August 26 declaring allowable system loss a government-mandated pass-through cost that should not form part of power companies' gross sales for VAT purposes.
The ERC said the exclusion would apply prospectively once its resolution was published and the BIR issued the corresponding tax guidance.
What changes for consumers

System loss refers to electricity that is generated and paid for but is lost before reaching consumers, including technical losses in power lines and equipment and non-technical losses such as pilferage and illegal connections.

The BIR's relief does not remove the system loss charge itself. Consumers will continue to pay the portion of electricity losses that utilities are allowed to recover under Energy Regulatory Commission rules, as well as VAT on other taxable components of their electricity bills.
Utilities may recover only system losses within limits prescribed by the ERC. Losses beyond those caps cannot be passed on to consumers and must be absorbed by the distribution utility.
Under the new tax treatment, consumers will continue paying the allowable system loss charge itself, but the additional 12% VAT previously imposed on that portion of the bill will be removed.

VAT will continue to apply to taxable generation, transmission and distribution charges. But, Mendoza said, this "means a lower amount will be passed on to consumers on covered billings and transactions."
The BIR directed generation companies, NGCP and distribution utilities to separately identify allowable system loss charges in billing and related documents.
Marcos sought broader relief
The change addresses only the VAT imposed on system loss charges, falling short of President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.'s broader call to remove the system loss charge itself from consumers' bills.

During his fifth State of the Nation Address in July, Marcos urged Congress to amend the Electric Power Industry Reform Act, or EPIRA, to prohibit utilities from passing system losses, including the corresponding VAT, on to consumers.
"Pinapasa ito sa consumer at kinakarga sa bill na pinapatungan pa ng value-added tax. Hindi naman kasalanan ng consumer kung bakit nagkaroon ng system loss," Marcos said.
("It is passed on to consumers and included in their bills, where it is also subjected to value-added tax. Consumers are not responsible for the system loss.")

Removing the underlying system loss charge would require broader changes to the existing regulatory framework. For now, consumers will still shoulder allowable system losses but without the VAT previously added to them.

articles.title: SC: No admin sanctions for LGU employee assigned to lower court without approval
articles.summary: The Supreme Court (SC) has said it cannot impose administrative sanctions on a locally funded employee, or an individual employed and paid by a local government unit (LGU), if it did not approve the…

blocks.text: Published September 14, 2026 4:48pm

The Supreme Court (SC) has said it cannot impose administrative sanctions on a locally funded employee, or an individual employed and paid by a local government unit (LGU), if it did not approve the employee’s assignment to a lower court.

In an 18-page decision, the SC Third Division said Administrative Circular No. 28-2008 provides that no locally funded employee may be detailed to a court without the SC’s approval through the Office of the Court Administrator (OCA).
The SC said any detail made without such approval is considered illegal and void.
“Without a valid detail, the Court is precluded from exercising its power of administrative supervision, which includes the power to discipline, over such locally funded employee,” it said.
“The detail is patently void, hence the Court cannot exercise its disciplinary jurisdiction over a person whose relationship with the Court is legally nonexistent,” it added.

The case stemmed from a complaint filed by an individual who discovered that her marriage at the Municipal Trial Court in Cities (MTCC) of Baguio City had not been solemnized due to the employee’s failure to process it despite the complainant’s payment of a registration fee.
When the complainant threatened to sue her, the employee said the SC had no jurisdiction over her because she was employed by the local government.

The SC, however, said that while it could not impose an administrative sanction on the employee, it could still cite her for contempt for conduct that tended to impede, obstruct or degrade the administration of justice.

“Since the image of a court is necessarily mirrored in the official and personal conduct of all individuals working there, [she] should be made liable for her conduct which degraded the administration of justice and tarnished the reputation of the Judiciary,” it said.
The SC directed the Baguio City MTCC to initiate contempt proceedings against the former employee.
The SC also directed the OCA to reiterate to all judges the need to secure approval before locally funded employees are detailed to their courts.— MCG, GMA News

articles.title: Indonesian police investigate deaths of Australian man and two children in Bali as suspected murder-suicide
articles.summary:
Police in Bali believe the two young children died as a result of violence, while a 57-year-old man is believed to have taken his own life

Indonesian police are investigating the deaths of…

blocks.text: Indonesian police are investigating the deaths of three Australians who died in Bali over the weekend, with initial reports suggesting a father killed his two young children before taking his own life.
The man, 57 and his two children, aged seven and four, who are also Indonesian citizens, were discovered deceased in a bungalow in Kuta on Sunday morning.

According to Denpasar Police, a witness, 51-year-old Nur Khamid, received a phone call from someone claiming to be the victim’s wife at around 8.30am on Sunday. She was in Jakarta, and asked Khamid to check on the condition of her husband and family, who she had been unable to reach.
Khamid went to their bungalow and tried to look inside through a window, but “no activity or people were visible inside”, Denpasar Police said in its statement.

The witness then met the bungalow owner and both returned to perform a check before contacting the “neighbourhood head”, Kelian Lingkungan. Residents “knocked and pounded” on the door before it was forcibly opened, and the three bodies were located.
“Police officers arriving at the scene conducted a crime scene investigation and preliminary examination alongside the Denpasar Police Identification Team,” the statement read.
“From the initial external examination of the three victims, it is suspected that the two children died as a result of acts of violence, while [the father] is suspected to have died by hanging.”
The bodies are at Prof Dr IGNG Ngoerah Denpasar Central General hospital for further examination and handling.
Denpasar police chief, senior commissioner Leonardo D Simatupang, said Kuta Police officers were investigating the incident.

“Investigators are still conducting inquiries, including crime scene processing, examining CCTV footage at the scene, and questioning witnesses – including the victim’s wife – to determine the cause of death,” he said.
Simatupang said Kuta Police had taken a statement from the man’s wife and reviewed CCTV footage. They had also coordinated with the Australian consulate.
after newsletter promotion
A spokesperson for the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade confirmed it was providing consular assistance to the family of the three Australians.
“We send our deepest condolences to the family at this difficult time. Owing to our privacy obligations we are unable to provide further comment,” they said in a statement.

articles.title: Senate requests Sara Duterte's PNB, UnionBank records by September 17, 2026
articles.summary: The Senate impeachment court has ordered the Philippine National Bank and UnionBank to submit Vice President Sara Duterte's bank records by Thursday, September 17.

blocks.text: Published September 14, 2026 4:39pm
The Senate impeachment court has ordered the Philippine National Bank and UnionBank to submit Vice President Sara Duterte's bank records by Thursday, September 17.

Senate impeachment court presiding officer Francis Escudero said this is an extension of the initial timeframe the court provided, given the banks' request for more time to submit voluminous documents, and that the September 17 deadline is non-extendable.
The Senate impeachment court granted the prosecution’s request for the issuance of a subpoena for the bank records of the Vice President on July 20.

The prosecution intends to present these bank records of the Vice President as evidence to support Article 2 of the impeachment case, which argues that the Vice President should be impeached due to accumulated unexplained wealth through the following:

items: failure to fully and truthfully disclose all her and her spouse's assets, liabilities, and net worth in her statement of assets, liabilities, and net worth (SALN), including in her SALN for the years 2022, 2023, and 2024; and
failure to divest and instead willfully continued all her business interests during her tenure as vice president for the years 2022, 2023, 2024, and 2025

blocks.text: Last week, the House prosecution panel asked for Duterte's admission of authenticity and ownership of bank accounts, which the prosecution will present as evidence during her impeachment trial, saying she can make such an admission without compromising her defense.

Prosecutor Chel Diokno of Akbayan party-list made the manifestation in a 104-page request for admission that the prosecution submitted to the court and the defense during Day 23 of the impeachment trial of the Vice President. —LDF, GMA News

articles.title: Fuel prices keep climbing as big hike takes effect September 15
articles.summary: This is now the second straight large price increase, as the government considers suspending excise taxes on LPG and kerosene again

blocks.text: HIKE. A pump attendant fills vehicles with fuel at a gas station in Paco, Manila, on January 12, 2026.
Rappler
This is now the second straight large price increase, as the government considers suspending excise taxes on LPG and kerosene again

items: Starting September 15, fuel prices in the Philippines will increase significantly, with gasoline rising by P5.68 per liter, diesel by P4.31, and kerosene by P4.62.
The latest hike follows a previous increase and is compounded by ongoing global supply concerns, particularly in the Middle East, affecting oil markets.
Transport groups are protesting rising fuel costs, urging the government to provide more support for public utility drivers, while discussions on suspending excise taxes on certain fuels are ongoing.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.
MANILA, Philippines – Fuel prices are going up sharply again starting Tuesday, September 15, continuing another run of big pump price hikes as fuel markets remain under pressure.
The Department of Energy (DOE) on Monday, September 14 announced the following fuel price adjustments for the week of September 15 to 21:

items: Gasoline – increase of P5.68 per liter
Diesel – increase of P4.31 per liter
Kerosene – increase of P4.62 per liter

blocks.text: The adjustments will take effect on Tuesday, September 15.

blocks.caption: Photo from DOE.

blocks.text: Before the latest adjustment, the DOE price monitoring showed common retail prices in Metro Manila at P85.70 per liter for gasoline RON95, P80.10 per liter for gasoline RON91, P90.10 per liter for diesel, and P119.90 per liter for kerosene for the week of September 8 to 14.

blocks.caption: Photo from DOE.

blocks.text: The latest increase follows last week’s big fuel price hike, when gasoline rose by P4.69 per liter, diesel by P5.18 per liter, and kerosene by P5.58 per liter.

Transport group Manibela is also staging a nationwide transport strike on Monday, September 14, citing rising fuel prices. The group has called on the government to provide more relief to public utility vehicle drivers and transport workers, who are among the sectors most immediately hit by higher diesel prices.

The government has so far kept in place a fuel subsidy program for qualified public utility vehicle drivers, with the discount raised to P12 per liter starting August 15, and continuing through September.

The Department of Finance has also said excise taxes on liquefied petroleum gas and kerosene could soon be suspended again if the Department of Energy certifies that Dubai crude oil has breached the government’s $80-per-barrel trigger level.

Finance Secretary Frederick Go is waiting for the DOE certification before recommending the suspension to the Development Budget Coordination Committee, according to the DOF. If approved by President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., the move would revive the tax break for LPG and kerosene that was used earlier this year before it ended on July 8, after the DOE certified that Dubai crude had fallen below the threshold.

The latest fuel price hike comes as global oil markets face another round of supply concerns from the Middle East. Saudi Arabia shut down its East-West oil pipeline after an aerial attack, while the advance of Yemen’s Houthis along the Red Sea raised fears of further disruption to another key shipping route.

That adds to continuing concerns over the Strait of Hormuz, the narrow waterway between Iran and Oman that remains one of the world’s most important oil shipping routes. Any disruption to tanker traffic through Hormuz or the Red Sea can quickly affect global crude and refined product prices.

Local pump prices also remain well above levels seen before fighting involving Iran and US-Israeli forces broke out on February 28. In the last full week before the conflict, DOE data showed common retail prices in Metro Manila at P56 per liter for gasoline RON95, P54.70 per liter for gasoline RON91, P55 per liter for diesel, and P83.47 per liter for kerosene.

The Philippines is a net importer of petroleum products, making local pump prices vulnerable to global oil price swings, foreign exchange movements, regional refined fuel prices, and disruptions in international supply routes. – Rappler.com

articles.title: ‘My testimony is not for sale: Ex-justice Tang claps back at defense’s bias insinuations
articles.summary: Sara Duterte's lawyer, in a bid to shoot down the former Sandiganbayan justice's credibility, asks her if she is a 'Kakampink' or 'anti-Duterte'

blocks.text: TRIAL. Retired Sandiganbayan presiding justice Amparo Cabotaje-Tang takes the witness stand in the trial of Vice President Sara Duterte on September 14, 2026.
Senate screenshot
Sara Duterte's lawyer, in a bid to shoot down the former Sandiganbayan justice's credibility, asks her if she is a 'Kakampink' or 'anti-Duterte'

items: Former Sandiganbayan presiding justice Amparo Cabotaje-Tang faced challenging questions regarding her impartiality during the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte.
Defense lawyer Mark Vinluan questioned Tang's political affiliations and whether she had been promised anything for her testimony, to which Tang firmly denied any bias or offers.
Senator-judge Erwin Tulfo later emphasized the need to respect all witnesses, while Deputy Speaker Janette Garin criticized Vinluan's questioning style as rude.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

MANILA, Philippines – Former Sandiganbayan presiding justice Amparo Cabotaje-Tang endured questions that sought to challenge her impartiality during the defense’s cross-examination on the 24th day of the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte.

Defense lawyer Mark Vinluan, who interrogated Tang, pointed out on Monday, September 14, that the witness was appointed to the Sandiganbayan by the late former president Benigno Aquino III in 2012, and applied for a Supreme Court justice post four times.
“Were you ever disappointed at (former president Rodrigo Duterte) for not appointing you?” Vinluan asked.
“No, that is his exclusive prerogative,” Tang answered.
Vinluan explicitly asked whether Tang was “anti-Duterte,” but Tang insisted she is apolitical.
Later, Vinluan asked Tang whether she was “promised anything in return,” such as an ambassadorial post, for her testimony.
“No, Sir, and I will never testify if ever I was offered anything material or otherwise,” Tang said. “My testimony is not for sale.”

blocks.caption: ‘My testimony is not for sale: Ex-justice Tang claps back at defense’s bias insinuations

blocks.text: This line of questioning by the defense appeared to have prompted senator-judge Erwin Tulfo later in the trial to make a clarification with presiding officer Chiz Escudero.
“If there are similar retired justices, officials to testify in this court, must we still afford them respect because of their service?” Tulfo asked.

“Any and all witnesses… should be accorded respect,” Escudero said. “If I understand where you’re leading towards, the counsels, especially the opposing counsel, have the right and leeway to ask questions of a witness even if he or she is a retired witness in order to test the witness’ credibility or reliability.”
Deputy Speaker Janette Garin, who sat in the post-trial press conference by the prosecution, said she took offense at the line of questioning by Vinluan.

“(Tang) was there to interpret laws to the best of her capability and her experience, having been in government, in those positions for a long time,” Garin said. “In my view, in a Bagong Pilipinas (New Philippines), being ill-mannered is frowned upon, and earlier, I felt like Attorney Vinluan’s questions were slightly rude.” – Rappler.com

articles.title: Reform declines to say whether £72m donors returned to UK in time to meet 12-month limit
articles.summary:
Richard Tice says donations are legally compliant amid speculation on overseas rules proposed in Rycroft report

Reform UK’s deputy leader has declined to say when two crypto billionaires

blocks.text: Reform UK’s deputy leader has declined to say when two crypto billionaires who gave a combined £72m to the party returned to the UK, as the architect of a review into overseas donations said anyone here for less than 12 months would be subject to a limit on donations.

Richard Tice said that while he was completely confident Reform had complied with all current and proposed laws on donations, he could not say when Ben Delo returned to the UK from Hong Kong, or how much time the Thailand-based Christopher Harborne spent in Britain.
“I’m not their executive assistant responsible for their day-to-day diary,” Tice told BBC Radio 4’s Today programme when asked about the details of their UK residencies.
He added: “Everything we’re doing is in accordance with the existing rules and the rules of the legislation that’s going through parliament as we speak.”
The legislation referred to, the representation of the people bill, does not currently contain any overall cap on individual donations, after lobbying from Labour-backing trade unions.

In response to the mega-donations by Harborne and Delo, trade unions, MPs and donors have urged the government to look again at the bill. But in the wake of a report on overseas influence on UK politics by Sir Philip Rycroft, a former senior civil servant, Britons living overseas will be limited to giving a maximum of £100,000.

The bill, which goes further than some of Rycroft’s recommendations, sets out that the cap applies to anyone who was not UK-resident for electoral purposes for at least a year from March 2026, applying retrospectively once the bill becomes law.
Speaking to Today, Rycroft said that while he could not comment on the circumstances of Delo or Harborne, the residency rules would apply.

“What I do understand is that the way the law will work, it will implement my recommendation on a limit for Brits abroad, as it were. But there will also be rules on, if they return to the UK, how long they have to live in the UK before they can count as domestic donors.
“And my understanding is that they will have to be living in the UK for at least a full calendar year. Once they met that requirement, then they become essentially a domestic donor.”

Rycroft said his review concluded a cap on money from overseas-based British donors was important as it was harder to trace the origins of overseas money, and that it was “a question of fairness” in limiting the influence of “people who had chosen to take their wealth abroad and to be taxed abroad”.
after newsletter promotion

The two separate donations of £36m by Harborne and Delo, announced within 24 hours, are unprecedented in UK political history and will give Reform enormously boosted resources before the next election.
Delo was based in Hong Kong but has returned to the UK. Asked when, Tice said this had happened “many, many months ago”. Harborne is registered to vote in the UK, but also lives in Thailand.

Asked how he could know the donations were permissible under the new rules, Tice said Reform’s compliance department had looked into it. But he condemned the retrospective plans of the bill, telling BBC One’s Breakfast that it was the action of “a socialist government that wants to retrospectively change the rules and regulations in order to protect themselves from a bit of competition”.

Speaking to Sky News, the schools minister Georgia Gould said the way the bill had been drafted was deliberate. Gould said: “The rules have been very clear, and the reason why it was applied retrospectively is because the risk is if you didn’t do that, then lots of donations would suddenly start flowing through before the legislation.

“The really important thing is this was an independent report that looked into these really serious issues that many people are concerned about, foreign interference in politics, and we made very clear at the time that it would be retrospective for good reason.”

articles.title: Marcos on SC acquittal of Imelda: ‘It’s been hanging over our heads’
articles.summary: President Marcos says the decision will not affect his selection of a new chief justice

blocks.text: President Marcos says the decision will not affect his selection of a new chief justice
MANILA, Philippines — President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. says he’s “glad” that the Supreme Court overturned the Sandiganbayan’s conviction of his mother, Imelda Marcos, of graft.

The decision, made public on September 9, overturned the anti-graft court’s November 2018 decision that convicted the former first lady of seven counts of graft. In 2018, Marcos did not hold public office after losing the 2016 vice presidential elections, and was elected president in 2022.
The Sandiganbayan earlier sentenced Imelda to six years and one month, up to 11 years, for each count of graft.

Imelda, 97, is the wife of the late dictator Ferdinand Marcos Sr. The Marcoses are accused of stealing from public coffers while they were in office, which included martial rule from 1972 to 1981. Marcos Sr. continued his authoritarian rule until he was ousted by the People Power Revolution in 1986

Imelda’s now-overturned conviction was in relation to her management of seven Swiss foundations. The Office of the Ombudsman found that over $200 million in public funds were involved in those private organizations.
The Supreme Court overturned the Sandiganbayan’s decision because the latter supposed erred when it deemed the Swiss documents as duly authenticated.

Marcos, who will be selecting a new head of the Supreme Court when Chief Justice Alexander Gesmundo retires in November 2026, says the decision on his mother’s case would not factor in his choice. “That will never enter our thinking in any way,” he told media on September 13. – Rappler.com

blocks.text: North Korea said Monday that its recent "live-fire" drill demonstrated "huge destructive power."

During the test on Saturday, different types of weapons were fired simultaneously, with the aim of boosting the morale of North Korean troops and improving their capabilities to "completely collapse the enemy," according to the state news agency KCNA.
KCNA reported that the drill involved five army ​units and tested attack drones, tactical cruise missiles, tactical ballistic missiles, and other weapons systems.

Experts say North Korea is not slowing down its weapons activities, even after US President Donald Trump recently scaled back a military exercise with South Korea in an apparent effort to revive diplomacy with leader Kim Jong Un.

blocks.caption: The drills came after the US, Japan and South Korea wrapped up maritime exercisesImage: Yonhap News Agency/picture alliance

blocks.text: North Korea claims great military power

North Korean Marshal Pak Jong Chon was cited by KCNA as saying the drill intended to "improve the level of specialization to bring down the enemy's armed forces organizationally and structurally once an order is issued." He added that the mobilized weapons systems demonstrated "the huge destructive power of concentrated fire."
South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff said several missiles were fired on Saturday and traveled about 250 kilometers (155 miles) into North Korea's eastern waters.
The distances indicate that the weapons are designed to strike targets in South Korea, including US military bases.
Why a new Russia-North Korea road bridge worries Ukraine
North Korea's response to 'provocations'
The firing drill came a day after the United States, South Korea, and Japan concluded a trilateral military exercise that North Korea considers a provocation.

In August, Trump ordered the Pentagon to "substantially reduce" the Ulchi Freedom Shield exercise conducted jointly with South Korea. According to the US president, the decision was due to his good relationship with Kim Jong Un.
North Korea rejected Trump's move, saying that shortening the exercise did not change its "provocative, aggressive nature."
The exercise ended six days earlier than originally scheduled.

Experts say Kim Jong Un likely believes his position in any potential diplomacy with the US has improved since his first meetings with Trump in 2018 and 2019. Kim said earlier this year that he could return to talks if the US abandons its "hostile policy" toward his country and recognizes what he calls North Korea's status as a nuclear state.

articles.title: Health advocates demand solutions to years-long TB drug shortage
articles.summary: Mass TB drug shortages have been reported since the last quarter of 2023 due to multiple failed and canceled biddings

blocks.text: STOCKOUT. Florita Dalida, founder of TB HEALS, speaks in front of health experts and advocates about on-the-ground TB drug shortage reports across 18 regions during a roundtable discussion on August 25, 2026.
Doctors Without Borders/Médecins Sans Frontières
Mass TB drug shortages have been reported since the last quarter of 2023 due to multiple failed and canceled biddings

items: Health groups in the Philippines are raising concerns over ongoing shortages of TB medicines, urging the Department of Health to treat this issue as a national emergency.
Advocates are calling for improved drug procurement schedules, better coordination among health regions, and a commitment from the DOH to ensure free and accessible TB treatment for all patients.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

MANILA, Philippines – Health groups and affected communities sounded the alarm over continuing shortages of tuberculosis (TB) medicines in the Philippines, urging the Department of Health (DOH) to develop efficient solutions to prevent delays in healthcare delivery.

Florita Dalida, founder of TB Health Education and Livelihood Support Community, Inc. (TB HEALS), told Rappler on Monday, September 14, that shortages or stockouts of TB medicine should be treated as a national emergency, as TB is highly contagious.
“Dahil tayo ay top 3 sa buong mundo na contributor ng TB cases, [imagine] kung ilan ‘yung kayang magkaroon ng TB habang hinihintay natin na mag-treatment sila,” she told Rappler.
(Because we are the third-highest contributor to TB cases worldwide, imagine how many Filipinos can acquire TB while we wait for them to be treated.)

Mass TB drug shortages or stockouts — specifically, first-line medications for drug-susceptible patients — have been reported since the last quarter of 2023 due to the DOH’s multiple failed and canceled TB drug biddings. All unsuccessful procurement activities, despite rebiddings, amounted to P2 billion.
Dalida added that it’s a “national concern” because of the procurement problems of the DOH. It’s the DOH, she said, that should purchase all allocations of “first-line drugs.”

Chris Muñoz, president of the Philippine Alliance of Patient Organizations (PAPO), said on Sunday, September 13, the DOH should recalibrate its drug distribution process to prioritize local government units and strengthen reimbursements, too, from the Philippine Health Insurance Corporation (PhilHealth).

Diagnosis and treatment are free through PhilHealth’s TB-DOTS (Directly Observed Treatment Short-course) package, valued at more than P7,000 in total. Case rates are also available for reimbursement, from P12,000 to P19,000 depending on the condition.
“The choice of where to seek care should belong to the patient, not the healthcare facility,” Muñoz said.

The Philippines has had the highest number of people infected with TB per 100,000 population in Southeast Asia since 2013. In 2024, the country has the third-highest TB burden in the world, after Indonesia and India.
Ironically, TB is preventable and highly treatable with fixed medication. TB treatment is free in all government-run health facilities nationwide.
When medicines are unavailable, patients may be forced to pay for treatment out of pocket, while treatment delays could increase the risk of transmission.

Louie Zepeda-Teng, president of TBPeople Philippines and a TB survivor, said on Friday, September 11, that she has been encountering reports of TB drug shortages across various regions during their community work.

She mentioned Tondo in Metro Manila, Rizal, Cavite, Bicol, Tacloban, Tawi-Tawi, and Cotabato as some of the areas they visited that had shortages — to the extent that health centers became hesitant to screen people for TB because they had no available medicine.

“I visited some places in Manila where I was told not to bother with medical missions and screenings, or even give talks at X-ray events for Manila residents, because supposedly there was no medication available anyway,” Zepeda-Teng said in Filipino.

Dalida also mentioned in a separate interview on August 29 that their data from the community feedback platform KomuKonek showed 30 reports of TB drug shortages in nine regions between 2025 and August 2026.
Zepeda-Teng asserted that the DOH should strengthen its commitments to lowering the number of cases, following its own roadmap to TB eradication.

“When we commit to this being free, you’re supposed to make sure na walang mamamatay dito (that no one will die). Kasi nga [pinangako mong] libre ito (Because you promised that this will be free),” she said.
In a roundtable discussion about TB stockouts on August 25, TBPeople Philippines shared an “urgent” appeal letter to stop recurring shortages, addressed to Health Secretary Edwin Mercado.
They asked to:

items: Improve the schedule of first-line drug procurement and not disturb the 16-million screening target for 2026
Strengthen coordination with all 18 regions through more accurate reporting of needed supplies
Have stronger mandatory notification and increase preventive treatment
Not to limit procurement access at the national level by encouraging LGUs to plan for universal healthcare funds and not just rely on national delivery

blocks.text: Dalida added that since the bureaucracy had already been identified as the root cause of the shortages, the DOH should realign with all concerned agencies to address it.
She said in Filipino, “I hope they fix the system. They should talk amongst themselves and prioritize those who have TB.” – Rappler.com

articles.title: One Nation’s plan to cut migration by 750,000 would ‘smash economy’ and force hospitals to close, Labor says
articles.summary: Universities Australia says party can’t take skills and jobs out of the country and ‘pretend there will be no consequences’

blocks.text: One Nation’s latest immigration policy would “smash the Australian economy” and force hospitals and aged care facilities to close, Labor has warned, while the university sector has urged against a “race to the bottom” on cutting overseas arrivals.
One Nation said on Monday it would cut the number of temporary migrants in Australia by more than 750,000 over three years, targeting international students and family members of skilled migrants.
The One Nation leader, Pauline Hanson, claimed the new policy would “reset” Australia’s immigration system and help ease pressure on housing and public services.

Temporary visa numbers would be returned to 2017 levels, under what Hanson says would represent a net-negative arrivals rate for the first three years. That would mean the net overseas migration (Nom) total would be 130,000 under the One Nation plan.
The home affairs minister, Tony Burke, said a halt on immigration “would smash the Australian economy” and warned regional communities would be the first to suffer.
“Hospitals and aged care facilities would be forced to close,” he said.
“There’d be a chronic shortage of backpackers to work in hospitality and tourism, or to help farmers pick their crops.
“The construction sector would grind to a halt. Regional universities would have to radically shrink or go broke.”
Burke said Hanson should be honest and upfront with Australians about the effect of the new policy.

Luke Sheehy, the chief executive of peak body Universities Australia, said the plan would do lasting damage. He said One Nation was joining Labor and the Coalition in a “race to the bottom” with plans to dramatically cut student visas.
“You can’t take skills, jobs and billions of dollars of economic activity out of the country and pretend there will be no consequences,” he said.

“International education is one of Australia’s biggest exports. It supports jobs across the economy, helps build the skilled workforce we desperately need and strengthens our relationships around the world.
“It also helps keep our universities going.”
Immigration debate

Hanson’s announcement comes as Labor and the Coalition consider new cuts to overseas arrivals, in an increasingly charged contest before the next federal election. Hanson will hope her plan plays well in the lead-up to the Victorian state election, due in November.

“I know Australians are doing it tough,” Hanson said. “Families are competing with hundreds of people for rental accommodation. Patients are stuck in ambulances because there are not enough hospital beds. Young Australians are being locked out of home ownership while wages and infrastructure fail to keep up.”

The target is to reduce student visa numbers, including visas for accompanying family members, to 350,000 over three years. According to education department data, about 680,000 international students studied in Australia between January to May this year.
A single student graduate program visa will be created, with numbers capped at 20,000 new visas per year. One Nation’s target is to reduce graduate visa numbers from 270,000 to 40,000.

The policy could also drive division within One Nation, with the lower house MP David Farley previously expressing concern that big cuts to immigration could deny his electorate of Farrer the workers needed to care for elderly people and work on farms.
Hanson said One Nation would give “illegal migrants” three months to leave, with those who departed voluntarily would be allowed to apply for visas in the future.
“Those who remain unlawfully after this period will be subject to immigration enforcement and a lifetime ban from re-entering Australia,” she said.
The Pacific labour mobility scheme for agriculture would remain in place under One Nation’s plan but temporary skilled migrants would lose the ability to apply for visas for family members.
“We will take back control of who comes here and how many we accept, train more Australians, restore living standards and put the safety and security of Australians first.”
after newsletter promotion
The prime minister, Anthony Albanese, and the opposition leader, Angus Taylor, have held talks on Labor’s delayed migration package. It is expected to further drive down net overseas migration.
But Labor has struggled to finalise the plan and delayed its announcement by more than a month.
Australian businesses ‘at risk’
One Nation’s policy was widely criticised by business groups.
Business Council of Australia boss Bran Black warned One Nation migrants were needed for growth in the economy.

“The starting point for any conversation with respect to migration cannot simply have the objective of cutting numbers, it has to be, how do we go about delivering the growth that ultimately locks in and secures our way of life,” he said.
Australian Chamber of Commerce and Industry chief executive Andrew McKellar said the business community would not support damaging cuts.
“Many Australian businesses would be put at risk by major cuts to the migration program. Pubs, cafes, hotels, and accommodation providers desperately need chefs.

“Aged care homes and hospitals are short of staff already. Farmers and resources sector businesses continue to face persistent workforce shortages. Housing projects are being held up, while others remain unviable because of lack of workforce and skills shortages.”
National Farmers’ Federation boss Hamish McIntyre warned food prices could rise due to worker shortages.
“One in seven employees on our farms across regional Australia now are working holidaymakers or backpackers,” he told Channel Nine.
“We need these people now.

“It’ll prohibit us from planting some of these crops. We rely on these people. We won’t be able to take the risks to spend all the money, we spend up front obviously to produce these crops, so we’re not going to take a risk if we can’t harvest them.”
Taylor dismissed the policy as “absolute nonsense”.

“I’m interested to know the details of One Nation’s plan. I don’t know what their non-numbers were. A few days ago, their immigration numbers were 130,000. Now it’s something different. Well, what is it, each year over the next three or four years?
“What are those numbers? They’re not in their releases. They need to explain it.”

MANILA, Philippines – Shoppers and commuters can expect Market! Market! to remain in operation well beyond 2027, after the Bases Conversion and Development Authority (BCDA) extended the lease of Ayala Land-led Station Square East Commercial Corporation (SSECC) by another 12 years and seven months.

Under the agreement, SSECC will continue operating Market! Market! for another 12 years and seven months beginning June 5, 2027, effectively extending its lease until January 2040, while Ayala Land commits P1 billion to modernize the BGC mall and prepare it for integration with the future Metro Manila Subway.

The subway’s Bonifacio Global City Station will be located within the Market! Market! property, effectively putting the commercial center at the center of one of BGC’s biggest planned transport upgrades.

blocks.caption: MAP: Metro Manila Subway stations

blocks.text: “For us, renewal does not simply mean building something new. It means looking again at the places we already have, understanding how cities and communities have changed around them and investing in them so they can create even more value for the next generation,” Ayala Land president and CEO Anna Ma. Margarita “Meean” Dy said in a press release on Monday, September 14.

The companies did not provide a detailed breakdown of the P1-billion investment, including which parts of the mall will be renovated or how construction could affect shoppers, tenants, and commuters. (READ: The renovation is done. Now Ayala is changing the shops inside its malls.)

Part of the property, however, is already expected to change as BCDA develops the area around the subway station. The agency said its transit-oriented development plans will repurpose a portion of Market! Market!’s Central Plaza as the site evolves into a transport hub connecting rail, road, commercial establishments, and workplaces.
BCDA President and CEO Joshua Bingcang said integrating the subway into the property would allow Market! Market! to continue serving as a gateway into BGC.

Market! Market! traces its roots to Ayala Land’s 2000 master plan for what was then called “Convergence Square,” envisioned as a mixed-use development combining retail, public transport, and civic space. Ayala Land disclosures show that the original agreement with BCDA covered a 25-year lease, renewable for another 25 years, with a P700-million upfront payment plus annual lease payments with fixed and variable components.

The mall eventually opened in September 2004 and has since become one of BGC’s oldest major commercial centers. Its original lease was due to expire in 2027, prompting earlier uncertainty over the property’s future before BCDA and Ayala Land agreed on the new 12-year-and-seven-month extension. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Oil prices rise after drone attacks shut down Saudi Arabia’s East-West pipeline
articles.summary: Price spike comes as rebel Houthis in Yemen target oil infrastructure and capture strategic island in Bab al-Mandab strait

blocks.text: Oil prices have climbed above $107 a barrel after a series of drone attacks forced Saudi Arabia to close its east-west crude pipeline.
Brent crude, the international benchmark for oil prices, surged to as much as $108 a barrel at one point on Monday, later easing back to $107.7 – a 3% increase on the day.

The spike came after Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthi forces launched several attacks against Saudi Arabia and captured the strategic island of Perim in the Bab al-Mandab strait on Sunday, expanding their control of the waterway.

Market concerns were also fuelled by the Gulf states postponing a meeting with Tehran to discuss creating a temporary shipping lane through the strait of Hormuz, a vital channel through which a fifth of the world’s oil and gas supply normally passes.
Traders in the kingdom have warned it will run out of oil stocks for export if it does not reopen the east-west pipeline within days.
Gas prices also climbed higher on Monday, with the UK benchmark rising by 5% to 208.73p a therm – its highest level since December 2022.

Energy prices have surged this year, as the US-Israel war with Iran has disrupted oil and gas supply across the Middle East. The oil price peaked at $126 in April but later fell back over the summer amid hopes of a lasting ceasefire.

The price then began to climb again after the memorandum of understanding between the US and Iran fell apart. After a fresh stepping up of hostilities the benchmark again rose above the $100 a barrel threshold last week for the first time since July.
Chris Beauchamp, of the broker IG, said that a “move back to the spring highs” looked increasingly likely.
“Oil markets are being subjected to their worst fears all at once – attacks on energy infrastructure, the closure of Hormuz and a breakdown in attempts to restart negotiations,” he said.
after newsletter promotion
“The risk of further disruption is also spreading beyond the Gulf, with the threat of renewed Houthi attacks on shipping adding another layer of uncertainty around key energy and trade routes.
“The major surprise is how calm markets remain in the face of all this, but if prices breach the March highs, things could get ugly very quickly.”

Oil output from Saudi Arabia had been under pressure before the attacks on its major pipeline. Riyadh told the Opec oil cartel recently that its crude production in August was at its lowest level since 1990, according to Bloomberg.

The spike in energy prices has triggered higher inflation across large economies around the world. Central bankers in the US, Japan and the UK must contend with the renewed rise in the cost of energy and accelerating price rises as they prepare to set interest rates this week.
